raw_response:
I farm small land and I have done it a long time, so I will keep the plan simple and spread risk instead of pushing everything into one crop. Because my main system is wheat-maize and I have well irrigation, I will keep most of my land in that rotation for steady grain and feed value. I will still keep some cotton because I know how to manage it and it gives me a cash crop, but I will not expand it too much because it takes more labor across the season. I will put small areas into mungbean and red bean to diversify income, reduce risk from one bad market or one bad weather period, and make use of my experience with mixed cropping choices. Since I am 60 and the household is only two people, I will choose workable input levels, use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps stand and yield, irrigate with the well when the crop is most sensitive, and avoid overly intensive spraying. I will rely mostly on rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale, but I will plough for cotton where I want a cleaner, deeper seedbed.
